newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks end lower on strike concerns.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks end lower on strike concerns.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed down on Tuesday on the back of a labour strike at the island's monopoly gas distributor Shell Gas Lanka Ltd, which was called off only after the market closed, brokers said.

"Market sentiment weakened on gas strike news today," said Sanjeeva Gunewardena, manager institutional sales at Commercial Stock Brokers. "Except for a couple of large parcels, we did not see widespread participation."
The manufacturing sector was particularly affected by the strike. Dankotuwa Porcelain was down 1.25 to 28 rupees, Ceylon Glass Company came down one rupee to 23 rupees.
"It showed our industry's vulnerability to labour problems," said Mahendra Jayasekera, general manager of CT Smith.
An announcement that the strike was called off came too late for the market, which was down 5.3 points at the close of business. Losses outnumbered gains 34 to 13.
The Colombo Stock Exchange all-share closed at 625.6. Turnover was 17.4 million rupees, up from Monday's 7.7 million, but well below the average turnover of the month, brokers said.
"The market has been looking for direction for the past couple of days," said Gunewardena. "When the situation is like that, people adopt a wait-and-see attitude." --Mohan Samarasinghe (941) 434319
